description: Issue #883: a cross-vendor review of b3dbae4b3 (#841/#862) found seven EtlSchedulerService IgnoreQueryFilters() call sites reachable from HTTP controllers (_EtlJobController/_EtlRunLogController/EtlJobDefinitionVM) with no check that the caller-supplied jobId belonged to the caller's own tenant -- an IDOR letting tenant A's ETLAdmin read (DryRun's source-data preview rows) or operate on (TriggerNow/Reschedule/Pause/Resume/Abort/Enable/Disable) tenant B's job. Fixed via LoadJobDefinitionForCallerAsync, a shared private helper every affected method now funnels through: it applies a TenantCode == callerTenantCode predicate unless the caller explicitly passes declaredSystemQuery: true (the #843 contract, reused verbatim). This mutant neutralizes exactly that guard (`if (!declaredSystemQuery)` -> `if (false)`), so the tenant predicate is never applied and the helper reverts to pre-#883 behaviour -- unconditional IgnoreQueryFilters() with no ownership check -- for every method that routes through it (TriggerNowAsync, RescheduleAsync, DryRunAsync, and, via EnsureCallerOwnsJobAsync, PauseAsync/ResumeAsync/AbortAsync/DisableAsync). Checked against all six of #883's HTTP-reachable cross-tenant negative controls that route through this specific helper -- TriggerNow_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, DryRun_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, Pause_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, Resume_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, Abort_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, Reschedule_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected -- each of which seeds a job under tenant B, authenticates as tenant A's ETLAdmin, and asserts the cross-tenant call is rejected (404/400, matching the pre-fix 'not found' shape for a genuinely nonexistent id); with the mutant applied, every one of those calls instead succeeds against tenant B's job. SkipNext and RerunFromSnapshotAsync's own runLog lookup are NOT in this mutant's red_tests -- they carry their own independent `if (!declaredSystemQuery)` guards (EtlSchedulerService.cs, inline rather than routed through this shared helper) and are covered by their own existing/updated mutants instead. The green control, SkipNext_OwnTenantJobId_Succeeds, is unaffected by this specific line (SkipNext never calls LoadJobDefinitionForCallerAsync) and proves the mutation's build/test environment itself is not broken.
target_symbol: EtlSchedulerService.LoadJobDefinitionForCallerAsync -- the `if (!declaredSystemQuery)` guard before the TenantCode predicate is applied

#883: tenant A's ETLAdmin must not be able to dry-run

#883: tenant A's ETLAdmin must not be able to resume tenant B's job by id
#883: tenant A's ETLAdmin must not be able to abort tenant B's job by id
#883: tenant A's ETLAdmin must not be able to reschedule tenant B's job by id
